approachQuestion.prompt: A log is an integer sequence with labels in 0..m-1, where 1 ≤ m ≤ n. Return the lexicographically smallest subsequence containing each distinct label present in the log exactly once. Preserve original order; labels absent from the input need not appear. Example: [2, 1, 2, 0, 1] returns [1, 2, 0]. Choose the best approach.
constraints: The input is immutable; n is between 1 and 200,000. All integers, indices, counts, and arithmetic results fit in signed 64-bit machine words; comparisons and arithmetic have unit cost.
Input and returned output are excluded from auxiliary space. Working stacks, arrays, and copies count. No hashing is used.

options.text: Count remaining occurrences in an array of length m. Scan the log, decrementing the current count. Skip labels already in the chosen stack. Before adding a new label, pop larger tops only when their remaining count is positive, clearing their chosen flags. Then push and mark the label.
options.feedback: A larger top can be postponed only if another copy remains. Replacing it improves the first differing position; membership flags prevent duplicates without removing the only future opportunity for a label.

options.text: Skip labels already chosen; otherwise pop every larger top and add the current label, without checking remaining occurrences.
options.feedback: This may lose a required label. For [2, 1], popping 2 leaves [1], although both labels must appear.

options.text: Return the first occurrence of every distinct label in the order encountered.
options.feedback: Choosing an early copy can block a smaller start. For [2, 1, 2], [1, 2] is legal and smaller than [2, 1].

options.text: Enumerate all subsequences, retain those containing each present label once, and choose the smallest.
options.feedback: This is correct but explores an exponential collection of choices, far beyond what is necessary for the declared size.

feedback.reason: Use future availability and membership to decide when a smaller label may replace a chosen suffix.
details: Maintain remaining counts and chosen flags indexed by label, and a stack of distinct chosen labels. A larger top is removed only when it still occurs later. Already-chosen labels are skipped. Copy the final stack once into the result.

Pop a larger chosen label only if another copy remains later. Otherwise the lexicographically smaller prefix would lose required coverage. Chosen flags prevent duplicates while remaining counts certify recoverability.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For replace-if-label-returns, choose the tightest worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair. Let n be log length and m the declared label range size, with m ≤ n. Allocate two arrays of length m, plus a stack of at most m labels. Count initialization and the final copy; no hashing is used.
constraints: Stack push, pop, and top take amortized constant time using a growable array; each entry uses a constant number of words. Count the working stack, but exclude input and final output. No recursive call stack or hash table is used.

options.text: O(n log n) time, O(m) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: Fixed-universe counters plus a distinct-label stack support a linear scan.
details: Initializing the arrays costs O(m); scanning and all stack operations total O(n). The final copy costs at most O(m), so time is O(n) because m ≤ n. The allocated count and flag arrays give O(m) auxiliary space even if few labels occur.
